name: Vienna Game
tagline: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3: an attacking answer to 1...e5 built around f4.
description: A complete White repertoire against 1...e5 with 2.Nc3. Against 2...Nf6 you play the Vienna Gambit, 3.f4, and use the pawn on e5 and the half-open f-file to attack. Against 2...Nc6 you develop with 3.Bc4 and meet ...Bc5 with Qg4 against g7. The ideas repeat — fxe5 then d4 and Bd3, the queen on the d1-h5 diagonal, the fork trick Nxe5 and d4 — and many natural Black moves lose material on the spot.

chapters.name: Vienna Gambit: 3...d5
chapters.intro: This is the main line of the Vienna Gambit. After 3...d5 4.fxe5 Nxe4 5.Nf3 our pawn on e5 gains space and keeps Black's pieces off f6, and the f-file is half-open for our rook. Black's knight on e4 looks strong, so we challenge it with d4 and Bd3, or with Qe2 when Black pins with ...Bg4. Then we castle and play on the f-file. If Black takes on c3, recapture and play d4 to build the centre. Watch the e4 knight: when it is attacked twice and defended once, Nxe4 and Bxe4 win a pawn.

lines.name: 5...Be7 6.d4 O-O 7.Bd3 f5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 { Black claims the centre with a pawn of their own. } 2. Nc3 { The Vienna. The knight guards e4 and leaves the f-pawn free, so f4 can come next, like a King's Gambit with an extra piece out. } 2... Nf6 { The most common reply: Black develops and attacks e4. } 3. f4 { The Vienna Gambit. White hits e5 and plans fxe5, which gains space and opens the f-file. } 3... d5 { The best answer: Black strikes back in the centre instead of grabbing the pawn. } 4. fxe5 { Take with the f-pawn. The pawn on e5 takes f6 away from Black's pieces, and our rook will use the half-open f-file. } 4... Nxe4 { The only good square: the knight jumps into the hole on e4. } 5. Nf3 { Develop and guard e5. Next d4 and Bd3 (or Qe2) to challenge the strong knight on e4. } 5... Be7 6. d4 { Builds a big centre and supports e5. Now Bd3 will hit the e4 knight. } 6... O-O 7. Bd3 { The e4 knight is now attacked twice and defended only by the d5 pawn. Black has to protect it, trade it or lose a pawn. } 7... f5 { Black supports the knight with a pawn. } 8. exf6 { Take en passant. The f-file opens for our rook as soon as we castle. } 8... Bxf6 9. O-O { Castled, with the rook already on the open f-file. The position is balanced and easy to play: Ne2, c3 and Qe1 or Bf4 follow, with pressure on e4 and d5. }

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5 4. fxe5 Nxe4 5. Nf3
quiz.question: What is White's main plan in this position?
options: d4 and Bd3 to challenge the e4 knight, then castle and use the f-file
Qh5 and a quick attack on f7
Nxe4 at once, winning a pawn
g4 and g5 to attack the king
quiz.explanation: The e4 knight is Black's best piece. d4 builds the centre and supports e5, Bd3 attacks the knight, and after castling our rook is already on the half-open f-file.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5 4. fxe5 Nxe4 5. Nf3 Be7 6. d4 O-O 7. Bd3
quiz.question: What must Black take care of now?
options: The e4 knight: it is attacked twice and defended only once
Nothing, Black can play any developing move
quiz.explanation: Our knight and bishop both hit e4 and only the d5 pawn defends it. A move like ...Nc6 loses a pawn to Nxe4 dxe4 Bxe4; ...f5 or ...Bf5 keeps it protected.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5 4. fxe5 Nxe4 5. Nf3 Bg4 6. Qe2 Nc5 7. d4 Ne6
quiz.question: What is White's strongest move?
quiz.explanation: The queen gives check on the e8-a4 diagonal and attacks b7 at the same time. After ...c6, Qxb7 wins a pawn.

chapters.name: Vienna Gambit: 3...exf4
chapters.intro: Taking the pawn is natural but risky. 4.e5 kicks the f6 knight, and only ...Ng8 is good: ...Nh5 and ...Ng4 hang the knight to our queen on the d1-h5 diagonal, and ...Ne4 simply drops it to Nxe4. After 4...Ng8 we play Nf3, d4 and win the f4 pawn back with Bxf4, often with Qe2 to put pressure on the e-file. We end up with a big centre and a lead in development while Black's knight is back on g8.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 exf4 4. e5
quiz.question: Where should the attacked knight on f6 go?
quiz.explanation: On h5 and g4 the knight is taken by our queen along the d1-h5 diagonal, and on e4 it falls to Nxe4. Only ...Ng8 is safe, even though it costs time.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 exf4 4. e5 Ng8 5. Nf3 d6 6. d4 dxe5

options: 7.Qe2, with pressure on e5 and the e-file
quiz.explanation: The queen lines up against e5 and Black's king. Qxe5+ wins the pawn back, and Bxf4 regains the gambit pawn too.

chapters.name: Vienna Gambit Sidelines
chapters.intro: Not every player answers 3.f4 with ...d5 or ...exf4. Against 3...d6 we develop with Nf3 and play d4; Black is solid but passive. Against moves that leave e5 to its fate — 3...Nc6, 3...Bc5, 3...Bb4 — we take with fxe5 and the f6 knight has to run. After 3...d5 4.fxe5 the only good move is ...Nxe4. Other knight moves let us grab the centre with d4 or win material outright.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 Bc5
quiz.question: What is the strongest reply?
quiz.explanation: The f6 knight is attacked. If Black tries ...Nxe4, Nxe4 wins the piece, and the ...Qh4+ check is easily blocked with Ng3.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5 4. fxe5 Ng4
quiz.question: Black put the knight on g4 instead of e4. What should White do?
quiz.explanation: With ...d5 played, the c8 bishop defends g4, so Qxg4 loses the queen. d4 takes the centre, and the knight on g4 is offside.

chapters.name: 2...Nc6 3.Bc4
chapters.intro: Against 2...Nc6 we play 3.Bc4, aiming at f7. If Black plays ...Nf6 we protect e4 with d3 and keep f4 as our main plan; the play is calm and our pieces point at Black's king. Watch for ...d5: with our bishop on c4 and knight on c3, a black knight on d5 is attacked twice and often lost. If Black plays 3...Bc5, the queen jumps to g4 to attack g7, and Black has to find an awkward defence.

The knight guards e4 and leaves the f-pawn free, so f4 can come next, like a King's Gambit with an extra piece out. } 2... Nc6 { Develops and guards e5. Black keeps ...Nf6 or ...Bc5 in reserve. } 3. Bc4 { The bishop aims at f7, the weakest point in Black's camp. } 3... Nf6 { Develops and attacks e4. } 4. d3 { Protect e4 with a pawn. The f-pawn is still free, so f4 stays our main plan. } 4... Bc5 { Develops actively and aims at f2. } 5. f4 { The Vienna plan: hit e5 and prepare to open the f-file. } 5... d6 6. Nf3 O-O 7. f5 { Gain space and shut in the c8 bishop. quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. Qg4
quiz.question: What does 4.Qg4 attack?
options: The g7 pawn, which the f8 bishop used to protect
quiz.explanation: Once the bishop leaves f8, g7 has no defender. Black must defend with ...Qf6, ...g6 or ...Kf8, and each has a drawback.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. Qg4 Nf6 5. Qxg7 Rg8
quiz.question: Find White's move.
quiz.explanation: The queen takes on f7 with the c4 bishop behind it. The king has no square and nothing can take the queen: mate.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 d5 5. exd5 Nxd5
quiz.question: Why is 5...Nxd5 a mistake?
options: The d5 knight is attacked by our knight and bishop and defended only by the queen
quiz.explanation: After Nxd5 Black cannot recapture: ...Qxd5 drops the queen to Bxd5. White is simply a piece up.

chapters.name: Other Second Moves
chapters.intro: Black's other second moves are less common, but you will meet them. Against 2...Bc5 and 2...Bb4 we play Nf3 and attack e5. If Black defends it with ...d6 we play d4 or Nd5; if Black develops with ...Nc6 or ...Nf6 instead, Nxe5 wins a pawn, and against ...Nc6 the fork trick Nxe5 and d4 wins back the piece. Against 2...d6 and 2...c6 we take the centre with d4, develop quickly, and use our extra space.

Nf3 { Develop and attack e5. } 3... d6 { The right way to protect e5. } 4. d4 { Hit the centre and open lines for our pieces. } 4... exd4 5. Nxd4 Nf6 6. Bg5 { Pins the knight. quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Bc5 3. Nf3 Nc6
quiz.question: What is the fork trick here?
quiz.explanation: We give the knight for the e5 pawn, then d4 attacks both the c5 bishop and the e5 knight. One of them falls, so we win the piece back and keep a strong centre.

quiz.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 d6 3. d4 exd4 4. Qxd4 Nc6
quiz.question: What is White's most active answer?
quiz.explanation: The pinned knight cannot take the queen, so the queen stays in the centre and we develop with tempo.
